newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS-Spain,Portugal court convergence kudos.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS-Spain,Portugal court convergence kudos.

text.p: International investors keen to play the European convergence card should look to Spain and Portugal in preference to Italy, but risks with all the peripheral European markets remain, economists said on Monday.
"The spread between Italy and Spain is around 70 basis points, and there could be some mileage in that spread," said Ken Wattret, international economist at Paribas Capital Markets in London.
European Union economic and finance ministers (Ecofin) on Monday welcomed Portugal and Spain's economic convergence programmes to qualify for the European single currency.
Both countries' debt markets are on a roll.
The Bank of Portugal cut interest rates on Friday in a surprise early move ahead of this week's release of April inflation data.
Ten-year Spanish bond futures broke a contract high last week, and a Spanish rate cut is also expected this week, if April CPI data, due on Wednesday, are low.
Expectations of lower official interest rates in Italy, meanwhile, have receded, after the Bank of Italy failed to cut following low April inflation data.
BTPs weakened early on Monday, in line with a softer dollar.
In addition, Italian newspaper La Repubblica said on Sunday that the European Commission will send Italy a letter this week on how to reduce its budget deficit.
The newspaper said nine other European Union countries would receive similar advice from the Commission, but added: "The warning issued to Italy is the most severe".
"Spain and Portugal could be in a reasonable position to enter EMU in the first wave," said Wattret.
"There could be decoupling between Spain and Portugal and the Italian equivalent, and we have seen early signs of that."
Italian bonds were trading at a 162 basis point spread differential to Bunds at 1018 GMT, while Spanish bonds showed an 89 basis point yield gap.
But Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London, thought the fervour for Iberian bond markets was overdone.
He saw an upbeat week for Spanish bonds this week followed longer term by a static bonos/Bund spread of 90 basis points on a three month horizon.
Meanwhile, Italy could steal several pips from its spread to Germany and tighten to 155 basis points over the same period, Edmonds added.
"We have seen the Spanish market fully discounting a 25 basis point rate cut as early as Friday, while there is still a significant chance of a rate cut in Italy."
The release next week of Italian inflation data for May could be a trigger for a drop in Italian interest rates, Edmonds said.

Bullish sentiments emerging from Monday's Ecofin meeting are likely to be overshadowed by events in core Europe, which have more capacity to derail the European economic and monetary union (EMU) process, said Phyllis Reed, European bond strategist at Barclays de Zoete Wedd in London.
Germany will release half-yearly tax estimates this week.
A high shortfall in German tax receipts will have a knock-on effect on EMU confidence, Reed said.

The French political scene ahead of elections on May 25 and June 1 is also creating tension, she added, despite an improved performance for the ruling centre-right in the most recent pre-election polls.
"There is a significant risk that we run into a period of underperformance in all the peripheral markets," Reed said.
She saw the BTP/Bund spread widening to 200 or even 250 basis points over the next couple of months, while the bonos/Bund spread could stretch to 150 basis points.
